methods.name: LoHa
methods.full_name: LoHa (Low-rank adaptation with Hadamard product; FedPara parameterization)
methods.paper_title: FedPara: Low-Rank Hadamard Product for Communication-Efficient Federated Learning
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + \gamma\,(B_1A_1)\odot(B_2A_2),\quad B_k\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A_k\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}}\ (k=1,2),\ \gamma=\alpha/r;\ W_0\ \text{frozen},\ A_1,A_2,B_1,B_2\ \text{trained}
methods.locus: any linear or convolutional layer; popular on Stable Diffusion UNet/text-encoder (LyCORIS)
methods.structure: Hadamard (entrywise) product of two rank-r matrices; \mathrm{rank}(\Delta W)\le r^2 (FedPara Prop. 1) at the parameter cost of a rank-2r LoRA. Equivalently (B_1\odot_r B_2)(A_1^{\top}\odot_r A_2^{\top})^{\top}: a rank-r^2 factorization through row-wise Khatri-Rao products. Conv kernels can use a Tucker-style core variant (FedPara Prop. 3, use_effective_conv2d).
methods.mergeable_reason: ΔW is an explicit dense d_out x d_in matrix that can be added to W_0 after training.
methods.identity_at_init: HF PEFT: three factors Kaiming-uniform and one (hada_w2_b) zero so ΔW = 0; the original LyCORIS code uses normal init with one factor zeroed.
methods.key_idea: Entrywise-multiplying two low-rank matrices multiplies their ranks, so a LoRA-sized budget yields an update of rank up to r^2. Proposed for communication-efficient federated learning (FedPara) and turned into a fine-tuning adapter by LyCORIS.
methods.results_note: FedPara matches original-layer accuracy with 3-10x lower federated communication; as a PEFT adapter LoHa is benchmarked mainly for text-to-image customization in the LyCORIS study (ICLR 2024).

relations.note: each Hadamard factor is a LoRA product BA

methods.name: HiRA
methods.paper_title: HiRA: Parameter-Efficient Hadamard High-Rank Adaptation for Large Language Models
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + W_0\odot(BA) = W_0\odot(\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^{\top}+BA),\quad B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}};\ \text{no }\alpha\text{ scaling (paper Eq. 6, HF PEFT)};\ W_0\ \text{frozen},\ A,B\ \text{trained}
methods.locus: any linear layer of an LLM (attention and MLP projections)
methods.structure: Entrywise (Hadamard) modulation of the frozen W_0 by a rank-r matrix; \mathrm{rank}(\Delta W)\le \mathrm{rank}(W_0)\cdot r, so the update is generically high-rank. Equivalently an additive update \Delta W = W_0\odot BA.
methods.mergeable_reason: W_0 ⊙ (BA) is a dense matrix of W_0's shape and is folded into W_0 after training.
methods.identity_at_init: Both the paper and HF PEFT zero the d_out x r factor: paper Eq. 5 writes W_hi = AB with A in R^{d x r} zero-initialized and B in R^{r x k} Kaiming; HF zeroes hira_B (d_out x r) and Kaiming-initializes hira_A, so ΔW = 0.
methods.key_idea: Reuse the pretrained weight itself as one Hadamard factor: modulating W_0 entrywise by a low-rank matrix gives high-rank updates aligned with W_0 at LoRA's parameter cost.
methods.results_note: Reported gains over LoRA and its variants on commonsense reasoning, dialogue generation and mathematical reasoning with LLaMA-family models (ICLR 2025 oral).

relations.note: same parameter budget r(d_in+d_out), but rank no longer bounded by r

methods.name: ABBA
methods.full_name: ABBA-Adapters (learnable Hadamard product of two low-rank matrices)
methods.paper_title: ABBA-Adapters: Efficient and Expressive Fine-Tuning of Foundation Models
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + \frac{\alpha}{\sqrt{r_1r_2}}\,(B_1A_1)\odot(B_2A_2) = W_0 + \frac{\alpha}{\sqrt{r_1r_2}}\,(B_1\odot_r B_2)(A_1^{\top}\odot_r A_2^{\top})^{\top},\quad B_k\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r_k},\ A_k\in\mathbb{R}^{r_k\times d_{in}};\ W_0\ \text{frozen},\ B_1,A_1,B_2,A_2\ \text{trained}
methods.locus: any linear layer of an LLM
methods.structure: Hadamard product of two independently learnable rank-r_1 and rank-r_2 matrices (rank \le r_1r_2), executed without materialising \Delta W via the row-wise Khatri-Rao identity (B_1A_1)\odot(B_2A_2)=(B_1\odot_r B_2)(A_1^{\top}\odot_r A_2^{\top})^{\top}; rank-stabilised scale \alpha/\sqrt{r_1r_2}.
methods.mergeable_reason: The product is an ordinary dense matrix that can be added to W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: (B_1,A_1) initialised from the top-r_1 truncated SVD of W_0; B_2 = 0 and A_2 Kaiming-uniform, so ΔW = 0 at init.
methods.key_idea: Make both Hadamard factors learnable (HiRA fixes one to W_0), anchor one to the principal subspace of W_0, and use a rank-stabilising scale; the Khatri-Rao trick keeps memory at LoRA level.
methods.results_note: Reports state-of-the-art results on arithmetic and commonsense reasoning benchmarks across multiple LLMs, outperforming LoRA, HiRA and other PEFT baselines.

relations.note: ABBA makes both Hadamard factors learnable low-rank products; HiRA fixes one factor to the full-rank frozen W_0. ABBA's SVD init of B_1A_1 approximates W_0, so it starts near a HiRA-like update, but HiRA is not an instance of ABBA's rank-r_1 class
same function class (B_1A_1)⊙(B_2A_2) as LoHa; differs in SVD-anchored init and √(r1 r2) scaling
matched parameter budget, rank up to r_1 r_2

methods.verification_notes: arXiv v4 comment and OpenReview (ICLR 2026 Poster) confirm venue; scale alpha/sqrt(r1 r2) (Eq. 7), Khatri-Rao Theorem 1 and hybrid SVD+LoRA init (Sec. 3, Table 3) checked; ABBA cites FedPara; not in HF PEFT tuners.
corrections: relations[hira]: type generalizes -> competes-with, note rewritten ('generalizes' was wrong: W_0 is full-rank and frozen, so HiRA is not a special case of a learnable rank-r_1 factor)

methods.name: LoKr
methods.paper_title: Navigating Text-To-Image Customization: From LyCORIS Fine-Tuning to Model Evaluation
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + \gamma\,C\otimes(BA),\quad C\in\mathbb{R}^{u_p\times u_q},\ B\in\mathbb{R}^{v_p\times r},\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times v_q},\ u_pv_p=d_{out},\ u_qv_q=d_{in};\ W_0\ \text{frozen},\ C,B,A\ \text{trained (C optionally factorized: decompose\_both)}
methods.trainable_params: u_pu_q + r(v_p+v_q)\ \text{(right factor factorized, default when } r<\max(v_p,v_q)/2\text{)};\ r(u_p+u_q)+r(v_p+v_q)\ \text{(decompose\_both)};\ u_pu_q+v_pv_q\ \text{(neither factorized)}
methods.locus: any linear or convolutional layer; widely used for diffusion-model customization
methods.structure: Kronecker product of a small dense block C with a low-rank block BA: \mathrm{rank}(\Delta W)=\mathrm{rank}(C)\,\mathrm{rank}(BA)\le \min(u_p,u_q)\,r. Block sizes: paper Eq. 5 sets u_p = largest divisor of d_out not exceeding min(f, sqrt(d_out)); HF's factorization() returns (f, d/f) when f divides d and otherwise the divisor pair nearest sqrt(d) subject to the smaller factor \le f (default f = -1, i.e. near-square).
methods.mergeable_reason: C ⊗ (BA) is materialised as a dense matrix of W_0's shape and added to it.
methods.identity_at_init: HF PEFT zero-initializes the left Kronecker factor C (lokr_w1) and Kaiming-initializes the right factors, so ΔW = 0.
methods.key_idea: Ranks multiply under the Kronecker product, so a tiny dense block times a low-rank block gives a high-rank, block-structured update with very few parameters.
methods.results_note: Evaluated alongside LoRA and LoHa in the LyCORIS study of Stable Diffusion customization, which reports method-dependent trade-offs in fidelity, diversity and controllability rather than a single winner.

relations.note: with the right factor left unfactorized LoKr is exactly KronA's A⊗B

methods.name: KronA
methods.paper_title: KronA: Parameter Efficient Tuning with Kronecker Adapter
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + s\,(A_k\otimes B_k),\quad A_k\in\mathbb{R}^{a_1\times a_2},\ B_k\in\mathbb{R}^{b_1\times b_2},\ a_1b_1=d_{out},\ a_2b_2=d_{in};\quad \Delta W x = s\,\mathrm{vec}(B_k X A_k^{\top}),\ X=\mathrm{mat}(x)\in\mathbb{R}^{b_2\times a_2};\ W_0\ \text{frozen},\ A_k,B_k\ \text{trained}
methods.locus: parallel to attention/FFN weight matrices (KronA); KronA^B and KronA^B_res sit parallel to the whole FFN block
methods.structure: Single Kronecker product of two dense small factors; \mathrm{rank}(A_k\otimes B_k)=\mathrm{rank}(A_k)\,\mathrm{rank}(B_k), reaching full rank with O(\sqrt{d_{in}d_{out}}) parameters; forward pass by the vec-trick without materialising \Delta W.
methods.mergeable_reason: The weight-parallel KronA merges into W_0 like LoRA (zero added latency in the paper's Table 2); KronA^B / KronA^B_res are linear branches placed in parallel to the whole (nonlinear) FFN block, Y = FFN(X) + sX[A_k ⊗ B_k] (+ s_res X), so there is no single existing weight to fold them into (127%/136% latency).
methods.identity_at_init: One factor zero-initialized and the other Kaiming-uniform (a = sqrt(5)); the paper reports zero-init of one factor markedly improves results.
methods.key_idea: Replace LoRA's low-rank product by a Kronecker product, which is full-rank-capable for the same tiny budget and cheap to apply via reshaping.
methods.results_note: On GLUE with T5-base, KronA variants outperform LoRA, adapters and Compacter at comparable budgets, with KronA^B_res the strongest (at extra inference latency).

methods.name: PHM-Adapter
methods.paper_title: Compacter: Efficient Low-Rank Hypercomplex Adapter Layers
methods.formula_latex: h \leftarrow h + U\,\mathrm{GeLU}(Dh),\quad D=\sum_{i=1}^{n}A_i^{D}\otimes B_i^{D},\ U=\sum_{i=1}^{n}A_i^{U}\otimes B_i^{U},\ A_i\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n},\ B_i^{D}\in\mathbb{R}^{\frac{r}{n}\times\frac{d}{n}},\ B_i^{U}\in\mathbb{R}^{\frac{d}{n}\times\frac{r}{n}};\ \text{backbone frozen, adapters trained}
methods.locus: bottleneck adapters after the attention and feed-forward sublayers (Houlsby placement)
methods.structure: Bottleneck MLP inserted serially with residual connection whose down/up projections are PHM layers: sums of n Kronecker products (Kronecker rank \le n, i.e. rank \le n after Van Loan-Pitsianis rearrangement), reducing parameters by about 1/n.
methods.mergeable_reason: The adapter contains a GeLU nonlinearity in a new serial branch, so it cannot be folded into existing weights.
methods.identity_at_init: No exact zero-init guarantee is stated in the method section; like Houlsby adapters it relies on the residual connection with small-initialized adapter weights.
methods.key_idea: Learn the 'multiplication rule' of an n-dimensional hypercomplex algebra: a dense projection becomes a sum of n Kronecker products, cutting adapter parameters by ~n.
methods.results_note: On GLUE with T5-base, PHM-Adapter (n = 12) trains 0.179% of parameters and is competitive with full fine-tuning and standard adapters.

relations.note: replaces the adapter's dense projections by PHM layers

methods.name: Compacter
methods.full_name: Compacter (Compact Adapter with low-rank PHM layers)
methods.paper_title: Compacter: Efficient Low-Rank Hypercomplex Adapter Layers
methods.formula_latex: h \leftarrow h + U\,\mathrm{GeLU}(Dh),\quad D=\sum_{i=1}^{n}A_i\otimes(s_i^{D}t_i^{D\top}),\ U=\sum_{i=1}^{n}A_i\otimes(s_i^{U}t_i^{U\top}),\ A_i\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\ \text{shared by all adapters and layers},\ s_i^{D}\in\mathbb{R}^{\frac{r}{n}\times\rho},\ t_i^{D}\in\mathbb{R}^{\frac{d}{n}\times\rho},\ s_i^{U}\in\mathbb{R}^{\frac{d}{n}\times\rho},\ t_i^{U}\in\mathbb{R}^{\frac{r}{n}\times\rho}\ (\rho=1\ \text{default});\ d=\text{hidden size},\ r=\text{bottleneck};\ \text{backbone frozen}
methods.locus: bottleneck adapters after attention and FFN sublayers (Compacter++: after the FFN only)
methods.structure: Adapter projections are sums of n Kronecker products of shared 'slow' n x n matrices A_i with layer-specific rank-\rho 'fast' matrices s_i t_i^{\top} (low-rank PHM, LPHM).
methods.mergeable_reason: Serial bottleneck adapter with a nonlinearity; adds inference latency and cannot be folded.
methods.identity_at_init: Not specified as an exact zero-init; relies on the adapter residual connection as in Houlsby adapters.
methods.key_idea: Combine hypercomplex (Kronecker-sum) layers, cross-layer sharing of the slow factors, and rank-one fast factors to bring adapter cost from O(kd) to O(k+d).
methods.results_note: On GLUE with T5-base, Compacter (0.073%) and Compacter++ (0.047% of parameters) perform on par with full fine-tuning and outperform it on SuperGLUE and in low-resource settings.

methods.name: KRAdapter
methods.paper_title: Towards Higher Effective Rank in Parameter-efficient Fine-tuning using Khatri--Rao Product
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + \alpha\,\big[U\odot_{KR}V\big]_{1:d_{out},\,:},\quad (U\odot_{KR}V)_{:,j}=U_{:,j}\otimes V_{:,j},\ U\in\mathbb{R}^{k_1\times d_{in}},\ V\in\mathbb{R}^{k_2\times d_{in}},\ k_1k_2\ge d_{out};\ W_0\ \text{frozen},\ U,V\ \text{trained}
methods.locus: linear layers of vision-language models and LLMs
methods.structure: Column-wise Kronecker (Khatri-Rao) product truncated to d_out rows; with random factors it is almost surely of full rank, and its singular-value tail is heavier (higher effective rank) than Kronecker or low-rank updates. k_1=\lfloor\sqrt{d_{out}}\rfloor, k_2=\lceil d_{out}/k_1\rceil.
methods.mergeable_reason: The Khatri-Rao product is a dense matrix of W_0's shape.
methods.identity_at_init: U zero-initialized and V randomly initialized (Kaiming-style, negative slope 1/sqrt(k_1)), so ΔW = 0; the scale alpha is typically 0.1.
methods.key_idea: Target effective rank, not just algebraic rank: the Khatri-Rao product spreads energy over many singular directions at about the cost of a rank-16-32 LoRA.
methods.results_note: Reports gains on vision-language models up to 1B and LLMs up to 8B parameters, especially on unseen commonsense-reasoning tasks, with LoRA-level memory and compute.

relations.note: column-wise vs full Kronecker product; paper contrasts their spectra

methods.name: LoRETTA
methods.paper_title: LoRETTA: Low-Rank Economic Tensor-Train Adaptation for Ultra-Low-Parameter Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + \mathrm{TT}(\Delta W_{up})\,\mathrm{TT}(\Delta W_{down}),\quad \Delta W_{up}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ \Delta W_{down}\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}},\ \mathrm{TT}(M)[a_1,\dots,a_D]=G^{1}_{a_1}G^{2}_{a_2}\cdots G^{D}_{a_D},\ G^{i}\in\mathbb{R}^{r_{i-1}\times k_i\times r_i}\ (\text{LoRETTA}_{rep});\ \text{TT cores trained}

methods.name: LoTR
methods.paper_title: LoTR: Low Tensor Rank Weight Adaptation
methods.formula_latex: W_s = W_{0,s} + \alpha\,B\,G_s^{\top}A^{\top}\ \ (\text{paper, row-vector form: } Y = XW_s + \alpha\,XAG_sB^{\top}),\quad A\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{in}\times r},\ B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r}\ \text{shared by all layers } s,\ G_s\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times r}\ \text{layer-specific};\ \delta\mathcal{W}=\mathcal{G}\times_1A\times_2B

methods.locus: a stack of same-type matrices across depth (e.g. all W_q, all W_v)
methods.structure: Tucker-2 decomposition of the 3-tensor of updates stacked over layers: shared left/right factor matrices with a per-layer r x r core.

methods.structure: Low-rank plus sparse-residual update whose sparse support comes from a robust-PCA (GreBsmo) decomposition of W_0, combined with unstructured or structured pruning of the resulting weights for inference efficiency.
methods.mergeable_reason: W_0 ⊙ M + UV + P_Ω(S) is a single matrix of W_0's shape.
methods.identity_at_init: ΔW = 0 at init: the text sets V = 0 and S = 0, while Algorithm 2 sets U = 0, V ~ N(0, 0.02), S = 0 (the paper is internally inconsistent about which low-rank factor is zero).
methods.key_idea: Exploit sparsity twice: sparse-plus-low-rank structure in the update for parameter efficiency, and sparse final weights for inference efficiency.
methods.results_note: On BERT, saves about 25% inference FLOPs with 0.5% trainable parameters at comparable downstream performance.

both sparse-plus-low-rank updates

methods.name: SHiRA
methods.paper_title: Sparse High Rank Adapters
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + M\odot S,\quad M\in\{0,1\}^{d_{out}\times d_{in}}\ \text{fixed},\ \|M\|_0=r(d_{in}+d_{out})\ (\approx1\text{-}2\%),\ S\ \text{trained only on } \mathrm{supp}(M)
methods.locus: linear layers of LVMs (e.g. SDXL) and LLMs (e.g. LLaMA)
methods.structure: Static sparse coordinate mask on W_0 (implemented by gradient masking or as a separate sparse delta); masks: Struct (rows/columns plus diagonal), Rand, weight-magnitude, gradient, SNIP; the sparse update is generically high-rank.
methods.mergeable_reason: Only 1-2% of entries of W_0 are overwritten, so the adapter merges (and switches) by a sparse scatter.
methods.identity_at_init: S zero-initialized (HF PEFT default init_weights=True), so W = W_0. HF ships only the random mask built in; the paper's Struct/WM/Grad/SNIP masks can be supplied through a custom mask_fn.
methods.key_idea: Fine-tune 1-2% of the base weights directly: sparse updates are high-rank, switch quickly on device and interfere less when fused.
methods.results_note: Outperforms LoRA on LVM and LLM adaptation while enabling rapid adapter switching and multi-adapter fusion; the PEFT implementation uses up to 16% less peak GPU memory than LoRA.

methods.name: Sine-LoRA
methods.paper_title: Efficient Learning With Sine-Activated Low-rank Matrices
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + \tfrac{1}{g}\sin(\omega\,BA),\quad \sin\ \text{entrywise},\ \omega\ \text{(frequency)},\ g\ \text{(gain) fixed},\ B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}}\ \text{trained}
methods.locus: LoRA/DoRA target layers in LLMs and ViTs (also NeRF and 3D-shape networks)
methods.structure: Entrywise sinusoid of a rank-r matrix; the rank of \sin(\omega\,BA) grows with \omega (the paper gives a lower bound in terms of \omega), so the update is no longer low-rank.
methods.mergeable_reason: sin(ωBA)/g is a dense matrix computable after training and addable to W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: With LoRA's B = 0 initialization, sin(0) = 0 so ΔW = 0.
methods.key_idea: A fixed high-frequency entrywise nonlinearity raises the rank of a low-rank parameterization for free.
methods.results_note: Improves LoRA and DoRA at equal parameter count across ViT, LLM (e.g. LLaMA-3-8B commonsense reasoning, GLUE), NeRF and 3D-shape tasks.

relations.note: drop-in modification of LoRA's product
both raise rank with entrywise operations on low-rank matrices

methods.name: MiSS
methods.paper_title: MiSS: Revisiting the Trade-off in LoRA with an Efficient Shard-Sharing Structure
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + \mathrm{expand}(D)=W_0+E\,D,\quad E=\mathrm{diag}(\mathbf{1}_{s_1},\dots,\mathbf{1}_{s_N})\in\{0,1\}^{d_{out}\times N}\ \text{fixed},\ D\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times d_{in}};\ \text{efficient form: }\Delta W=D'\,(\mathbf{1}_{d_{in}/r}^{\top}\otimes I_r),\ D'\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r}
methods.locus: any linear layer of LLMs
methods.structure: A single small trainable matrix replicated across shards by a fixed 0/1 replication operator (a Kronecker product with an all-ones vector); rank \le N (or r).
methods.mergeable_reason: The expanded matrix is dense and is added to W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: D = 0 (paper and HF default 'balance' mode). HF stores the efficient-form matrix as r x d_out and computes y += (Σ_g x^{(g)}) D, i.e. ΔW = D^T(1^T ⊗ I_r); HF's 'bat' mode is a different, weight-dependent update inherited from Bone.
methods.key_idea: Replace one LoRA factor by a fixed shard-replication operator: a single zero-initialized matrix gives fast init, low memory and LoRA-level accuracy.
methods.results_note: Reports a favorable trade-off between performance, memory, initialization overhead and speed versus LoRA, PiSSA and DoRA on LLaMA-2, Mistral, RWKV and Qwen3.

notes: Scope: methods whose novelty is the algebraic/tensor-network SHAPE of Delta W beyond plain low rank. 29 methods in 8 sub-families: (1) Hadamard: loha, hira, abba; (2) Kronecker / hypercomplex / Khatri-Rao: lokr, krona, phm-adapter, compacter, kadaptation, kradapter; (3) tensor networks: loretta, tt-lora, lotr, fact, flora-tucker, lorta, metatt, quanta, quantum-peft; (4) square high-rank / block (direct-sum) shapes: mora, melora, gralora, bd-lora; (5) Monarch: more; (6) circulant: c3a; (7) sparse(+low-rank): rosa, dsee, shira; (8) entrywise-nonlinear or replication shapes: sine-lora, miss. Unifying algebra for the category-theory site: Kronecker product = tensor product of linear maps, so rank(A (x) B) = rank A * rank B (LoKr, KronA; MoRA's reshape variant is I (x) M); a sum of n Kronecker products has Kronecker rank at most n, i.e. ordinary rank at most n after the Van Loan-Pitsianis rearrangement, so PHM/KAdaptation are 'low rank in another matricization'; Hadamard product = Kronecker product restricted to the diagonal, A o B = J_m^T (A (x) B) J_n with J_k = [e_i (x) e_i]_i the diagonal embedding R^k -> R^{k^2}, hence rank(A o B) <= rank A * rank B (LoHa, HiRA, ABBA) and the row-wise Khatri-Rao factorization ABBA uses; Khatri-Rao = column-wise Kronecker (KRAdapter); block-diagonal = direct sum of maps (MELoRA, BD-LoRA, MoRA); a circulant is an intertwiner of the cyclic group's regular representation, diagonalized by the DFT (C3A and FourierFT both live in the DFT basis: C3A's blocks are DFT-diagonal, FourierFT's spectrum is sparse); TT, Tucker and CP adapters are string diagrams in FinVect with trainable boxes, differing only in the graph of contractions (chain, star, hyperedge). A useful invariant across the family is the rank of Delta W under a chosen matricization/reshaping, plus whether factors are shared across layers (LoTR, FacT, LoRTA, MetaTT, Compacter, KAdaptation). Ambiguities: 'FLoRA' names at least three different papers (this Tucker-core one, ICLR 2025, retitled 'Maintaining Structural Integrity...'; the gradient-compression Flora of Hao et al.; federated FLoRA), so the id is flora-tucker. ABBA exists (arXiv 2505.14238, retitled 'ABBA-Adapters', ICLR 2026). HiRA has no arXiv version (ICLR 2025 proceedings/OpenReview only). SHiRA is a sparse-selective method included as a seed; it also belongs in a selective/sparse family. BD-LoRA, MiSS and GraLoRA are low-rank-bounded or rank-k*r but included because their novelty is the shape constraint (block-diagonal, replication, block grid). Unverified details (medium confidence): initialization of MoRe, LoRTA, Quantum-PEFT and KAdaptation is not stated in the papers (MetaTT's is in its Appendix G); TT-LoRA's venue is from IEEE Xplore/Semantic Scholar (ICMLA 2024) and it does NOT start from the identity; LoRETTA's compensation of random init is paraphrased. Omitted for low uptake or because they duplicate a listed shape: Block Circulant Adapter (BCA, Ding et al., IJCAI 2025, arXiv 2505.00582; same block-circulant shape as C3A plus a learning-rate heuristic), DoTA (TT init from pretrained weights), TLoRA / transformed low-rank via tensor decomposition (ICCV 2025, arXiv 2501.08727), LSR-Adapt (Kronecker-sum kernels), SoKA (SVD on Kronecker adaptation), TT-LoRA MoE, Kron-LoRA. Hadamard Adapter (CIKM 2023, arXiv 2407.11033) is an activation-scaling method that belongs with (IA)^3, not here. Orthogonal butterfly/Householder methods (BOFT, OFT, HRA) and random-basis methods (VeRA, RandLoRA) and spectral FourierFT belong to other families and appear only as relation targets. Verification pass (2026-10-01): venues corrected for KronA (NeurIPS 2023 ENLSP-III workshop), MoRe (ICML 2024 ES-FoMo II / FM-Wild workshops), MiSS (ICLR 2026) and MetaTT (TMLR 2026); MoRA (ICLR 2025 withdrawn) and LoRTA (ICLR 2025 rejected) remain arXiv-only. KRAdapter is exactly LoHa with frozen 0/1 left factors (row-wise Khatri-Rao identity).
verification_summary: All 29 methods and 9 papers verified; none dropped. 33 arXiv ids batch-checked against the arXiv API (titles, first authors, first-version years all matched); HiRA has no arXiv version and was confirmed on OpenReview/ICLR proceedings; venues cross-checked with arXiv comments, OpenReview API, ACL Anthology, PMLR, NeurIPS/ICLR proceedings, Crossref and IEEE DOIs; every formula was checked against the paper PDF/HTML and HF PEFT v0.21.1 source (src/peft/tuners). Main fixes: venues of KronA, MoRe, MiSS, MetaTT; DSEE formula (mask prunes W_0, not W_0+ΔW); QuanTA fold-in sign (W_0 - S); BD-LoRA scaling (alpha/sqrt(r/N)); C3A HF 1/d_in factor; LoTR input/output factor convention; Quantum-PEFT exact circuit and parameter count; MetaTT init and exact count; relations abba->hira and metatt->lotr downgraded from 'generalizes' to 'competes-with', c3a->fourierft from 'dual-to' to 'competes-with', loha->kradapter upgraded to an exact 'generalizes'. 49 field-level corrections in total.
